1.caption: HTTP: Address
1.description: IP address or name (use numeric address if possible to bypass DNS lookup). Mainly used for  checks in the same network.

2.caption: HTTP: Basic Auth Credentials
2.description: Username:password on sites with basic authentication.

3.caption: HTTP: Host
3.description:
Host name argument for servers using host headers (virtual host)
Append a port to include it in the header (eg: example.com:5000)

6.caption: HTTP: SSL?
6.description: Connect via SSL. Port defaults to 443.

7.caption: HTTP: Expected String
7.description: String to expect in the content.

9.caption: Criticality
9.description: Defines if and when notifications are sent. A = 7x24, B = 5x12, C = never. Host criticality limits what its services can send. For example, given a host with criticality B, if a service with criticality A has a problem, the notification will only be sent during 5x12.

12.caption: HTTP: Certificate
12.description: Minimum number of days a certificate has to be valid. This parameter explicitely sets the port to 443 and ignores the URL if passed.

13.caption: HTTP: Client Cert
13.description: Name of file contains the client certificate (PEM format)

15.caption: HTTP: Critical Time
15.description: Response time to result in critical status (seconds)

16.caption: HTTP: Expect
16.description: Comma-delimited list of strings, at least one of them is expected in the first (status) line of the server response

18.caption: HTTP: Header
18.description: Any other tags to be sent in http header

19.caption: HTTP: Header String
19.description: String to expect in the response headers

20.caption: HTTP: Max Age
20.description: Warn if document is more than seconds old

21.caption: HTTP: Method
21.description: Set http method (for example: HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT, DELETE)

23.caption: HTTP: Page Size
23.description: Minimum page size required:Maximum page size required

25.caption: HTTP: Private Key
25.description: Name of file contains the private key (PEM format)

26.caption: HTTP: Proxy Auth
26.description: Username:password on proxy-servers with basic authentication

28.caption: HTTP: Useragent
28.description: String to be sent in http header as User Agent

29.caption: HTTP: Warning Time
29.description: Response time to result in warning status (seconds)

30.caption: HTTP: Invert Regex?
30.description: Return CRITICAL if found, OK if not

31.caption: HTTP: Ignore Body?
31.description: Don't wait for document body: stop reading after headers

45.caption: About Me: Tags?

48.caption: Acmesh Status: Brief?
48.description: Hide the rows that are within the thresholds and show only those in a WARN or CRIT state. Perfdata and alerting are unaffected: every item still emits performance data and still drives the overall check state, so this is safe to leave on.

49.caption: Acmesh Status: Critical
49.description: CRIT threshold for the time remaining until a certificate expires. Accepts a Nagios range in days (`5:`), a percentage of the total validity period (`10%`, CRIT when less than 10% of the lifetime is left), or a duration with a unit (`3d`, `12h`, `2W`, `1M`; CRIT when less time than that is left). Examples: `5:` `10%` `3d`.

50.caption: Acmesh Status: Grace Renewal
50.description: How long an overdue renewal is tolerated before it counts towards the state. Set this to cover the interval the acme.sh renewal job runs at, so a run that has not happened yet is not reported as a failure. Starts at the renewal time acme.sh recorded for the certificate. A duration such as `12h`, `8D` or `2W`; `0D` disables the grace period. Example: `--grace-renewal=8D` for a job that runs weekly.

51.caption: Acmesh Status: Ignore
51.description: Any item matching this Python regex will be ignored. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `(?i)linuxfabrik` for a case-insensitive match.

52.caption: Acmesh Status: Match
52.description: Filter by this Python regular expression. Case-sensitive by default; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching. Can be specified multiple times. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second). Examples: `(?i)example` to match "example" regardless of case. `^(?!.*example).*$` to match any string except "example" (negative lookahead).

53.caption: Acmesh Status: No Match Severity
53.description: State to report when no item matches the filters and nothing is checked.

54.caption: Acmesh Status: No Perfdata?
54.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

55.caption: Acmesh Status: Path
55.description: Directory acme.sh keeps its configuration in, the one it is called with as `--config-home`. The certificate store is read from the `CERT_HOME` recorded there, and from this directory itself where that names none. Example: `--path=/etc/acme.sh`.

56.caption: Acmesh Status: Severity
56.description: Severity assigned to a certificate whose renewal is overdue, whose installed copy is missing, which carries no issued certificate, or which is still deployed after having been detached from renewal. Each of these keeps the certificate valid for the time being, which is why they default to %(default)s; the expiry thresholds raise the state on their own as the deadline comes closer.

57.caption: Acmesh Status: Warning
57.description: WARN threshold for the time remaining until a certificate expires. Accepts a Nagios range in days (`14:`), a percentage of the total validity period (`25%`, WARN when less than 25% of the lifetime is left), or a duration with a unit (`10d`, `12h`, `2W`, `1M`; WARN when less time than that is left). Examples: `14:` `25%` `10d`.

59.caption: Aide Logfile: Critical
59.description: CRIT threshold for the number of differences (added, removed and changed entries together) that the last AIDE check found. Supports Nagios ranges. Example: `--critical=0` to get a critical alert on the first difference.

60.caption: Aide Logfile: Max Age
60.description: Maximum age of the report in hours. An older report means that the regular AIDE check no longer runs.

61.caption: Aide Logfile: No Perfdata?
61.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

62.caption: Aide Logfile: Warning
62.description: WARN threshold for the number of differences (added, removed and changed entries together) that the last AIDE check found. Supports Nagios ranges. The default alerts on the first difference.

68.caption: Apache httpd Disclosure: Severity
68.description: State to report for a server that discloses information. One of `warn` or `crit`.

70.caption: Apache httpd Disclosure: URL
70.description: Base URL of the Apache httpd server to inspect. Example: `--url=https://www.example.com`

72.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Auth Failures Critical
72.description: Number of authentication failures within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--auth-failures-critical=200`.

73.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Auth Failures Warning
73.description: Number of authentication failures within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--auth-failures-warning=20`.

74.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Client Denials Critical
74.description: Number of denied requests within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--client-denials-critical=200`.

75.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Client Denials Warning
75.description: Number of denied requests within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--client-denials-warning=50`.

76.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Critical Level
76.description: Least severe Apache log level that returns CRITICAL. Each level includes everything more severe than itself, so `error` covers `crit`, `alert` and `emerg` as well. Case-sensitive. `none` lets no level return CRITICAL, which leaves the events this check names as the only way to reach it. Example: `--critical-level=error`.

77.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Icinga Callback?
77.description: Ask the monitoring server whether the service running this check is acknowledged. Where it is, what this run reports is remembered as already handled, so it no longer raises an alert on the following runs. Requires `--icinga-url`, `--icinga-username`, `--icinga-password` and `--icinga-service-name`.

79.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Icinga Service Name
79.description: Unique name of the service running this check, as the monitoring server knows it. Take it from the `__name` service attribute. Example: `monitoring-server!my-service-name`.

82.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Ignore
82.description: Ignore a log line matching this Python regular expression. The log line is lowercased before matching, so write the pattern in lowercase (or use the `(?i)` flag). Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--ignore='ah01630'`.

83.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Insecure?
83.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes, which is the only network connection this check opens. This option explicitly allows insecure SSL connections.

84.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Lookback
84.description: Denied requests, failed passwords and failed requests are counted within this window rather than reported one by one. Time window in seconds to look back over, ending at the moment of the run. Only what falls within it is counted, so what is reported is how often something happened lately rather than a total that keeps growing for as long as the source is kept. Example: `--lookback=3600`.

85.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Match
85.description: Only consider a log line matching this Python regular expression. The log line is lowercased before matching, so write the pattern in lowercase (or use the `(?i)` flag). Can be specified multiple times. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second). Example: `--match='\[ssl:'`.

86.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: No Insecure?
86.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes, which is the only network connection this check opens. Verify the TLS certificate against the system trust store, overriding the insecure default of this check. Use it once the endpoint presents a publicly trusted certificate, or once its CA has been added to the system trust store.

87.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: No Match Severity
87.description: State to report when no item matches the filters and nothing is checked.

88.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: No Per Source?
88.description: Judge a rate by everything that arrived within the window, whatever source the lines name. Use this where the log reaches this check through something that rewrites or drops the address of the peer, or where every source is as interesting as the next.

89.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: No Perfdata?
89.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

90.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: No Proxy?
90.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes, which is the only network connection this check opens. Do not use a proxy, not even one the environment names. Overrides `--proxy`.

91.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Per Source?
91.description: Judge a rate by the busiest single source address rather than by everything that arrived. A handful of failures from one address within the window is somebody working on this host; the same number spread over as many addresses is the background of an open network going past, and only the first is worth reporting. Lines that name no source are counted together as one, so a burst of those still reports.

92.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Proxy
92.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes, which is the only network connection this check opens. Proxy to reach the target through. The scheme defaults to `http` when omitted. Overrides the proxy the environment names (`http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `all_proxy`) together with the exceptions it lists in `no_proxy`, and is itself overridden by `--no-proxy`. Without either parameter the environment applies. Credentials belong into the environment variable rather than here, because a command-line argument is visible to every user on the host. Example: `--proxy=http://proxy.example.com:3128`.

93.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Proxy Failures Critical
93.description: Number of unreachable backends within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--proxy-failures-critical=50`.

94.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Proxy Failures Warning
94.description: Number of unreachable backends within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. One of them is a backend being restarted, so this counts how many arrived rather than that any did. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--proxy-failures-warning=1`.

95.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Request Errors Critical
95.description: Number of failed requests within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. Counts what Apache logged about one request and one client, denied requests and failed passwords excluded, as those have counters of their own. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--request-errors-critical=200`.

96.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Request Errors Warning
96.description: Number of failed requests within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. Counts what Apache logged about one request and one client, denied requests and failed passwords excluded, as those have counters of their own. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--request-errors-warning=50`.

97.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Server Log
97.description: Log source to read from. Accepts a file path, `docker:CONTAINER`, `podman:CONTAINER`, `kubectl:CONTAINER` or `systemd:UNITNAME`. Can be specified multiple times, and everything named is then read as one window; a source named twice is read once. If omitted, the check reads the `ErrorLog` of the main Apache configuration file and of every virtual host it configures, falls back to the common locations of the distributions, and reads the journal of the Apache unit along with them; what they share is counted once. Example: `--server-log=systemd:httpd.service`.

99.caption: Apache httpd Logfile: Warning Level
99.description: Least severe Apache log level that returns WARNING. Each level includes everything more severe than itself, and a level that `--critical-level` already covers returns CRITICAL instead. Case-sensitive. `none` lets no level return WARNING, which leaves the events this check names as the only way to reach it. Example: `--warning-level=warn`.

101.caption: Apache httpd Security: Brief?
101.description: Hide the rows that are within the thresholds and show only those in a WARN or CRIT state. Perfdata and alerting are unaffected: every item still emits performance data and still drives the overall check state, so this is safe to leave on.

102.caption: Apache httpd Security: Command
102.description: Path to the Apache httpd control binary. Probed automatically if not given: `httpd` first, then `apachectl`. Must resolve within a standard binary directory (/bin, /opt, /sbin, /usr), and nobody but root may be able to change it or a directory above it. Example: `--command=/usr/sbin/httpd`

103.caption: Apache httpd Security: Ignore
103.description: Any check whose name matches this Python regex will be dropped from the report. The name is the one in the `Check Name` column of the table, not a module or a file name, and it is matched anywhere in that name, so the name as it stands is enough and needs no anchors. A filter that matches no check is reported rather than silently doing nothing. Use it for a finding the site knowingly accepts, for example the status module on a host whose monitoring reads it. Case-sensitive by default; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--ignore='Status module'`

104.caption: Apache httpd Security: Match
104.description: Only report the checks whose name matches this Python regex. Filter by this Python regular expression. Case-sensitive by default; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching. Can be specified multiple times. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second). Examples: `(?i)example` to match "example" regardless of case. `^(?!.*example).*$` to match any string except "example" (negative lookahead).

247.description: CRIT threshold for the time remaining until the certificate expires. Accepts a Nagios range in days (`5:`), a percentage of the total validity period (`10%`, CRIT when less than 10% of the lifetime is left), or a duration with a unit (`3d`, `12h`, `2W`, `1M`; CRIT when less time than that is left). Examples: `5:` `10%` `3d`.

248.caption: Cert: Exclude

249.caption: Cert: Extend Ports
249.description: TCP port to probe on every scanned target, appended to the default or the `--ports` list. Only applies to --source=scan. A range is written `start-end`. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--extend-ports=8443`.

250.caption: Cert: Filename
250.description: Path to a certificate file or a glob pattern matching multiple certificate files. Required when --source=file. Files are read as PEM or DER (autodetected); when a PEM bundle contains multiple certificates (typical for fullchain.pem or a CA bundle), each certificate becomes its own row in the output. Globs follow Python conventions: `*` matches one path segment, `**` matches across directories. Always quote the pattern in shells so that the shell does not expand the wildcard before the plugin sees it. Example: `--filename='/etc/ssl/certs/*.pem'`. Recursive example: `--filename='/etc/letsencrypt/live/**/cert.pem'`

251.caption: Cert: Host

252.caption: Cert: Insecure?
252.description: Skip chain and hostname verification entirely. The certificate is still fetched and inspected, but the chain verdict is reported as "verification skipped".

253.caption: Cert: Interface

255.caption: Cert: Max Workers
255.description: Maximum number of targets to scan in parallel. Only applies to --source=scan. Raising this shortens the run but multiplies the system time the kernel spends on connects to addresses where no host answers, which slows down every other check on the same host. Each worker also holds one socket, so the value is clamped to what the file-descriptor limit of the process allows. Default: derived from that limit, at most 200.

Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--ports=443 --ports=993 --ports=8000-8100`. Default: 443, 465, 636, 990, 993, 995, 3269, 5671, 5986, 6443, 8006, 8200, 8443, 8883, 9090, 9443, 10000.

Example: `--proxy=http://proxy.example.com:3128`. Only applies to --source=url.

261.caption: Cert: Severity

A valid self-signed certificate is always tolerated. Defaults to %(default)s so that operators running internal CAs are not paged by trust issues that are expected in their environment. Set to `crit` to enforce strict trust.

803.caption: Freeipa Logfile: Critical
803.description: Least severe ipa-healthcheck result that returns CRITICAL. Each result includes everything more severe than itself, so `ERROR` covers `CRITICAL` as well. Case-sensitive. `none` lets no result return CRITICAL. Example: `--critical=CRITICAL`.

804.caption: Freeipa Logfile: Ignore
804.description: Any ipa-healthcheck result matching this Python regex will be ignored. The regex is matched against the line the check prints for the result, `<source>.<check>[.<key>]: <message>`, without the result value. Case-sensitive. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--ignore=IPADNSSystemRecordsCheck`

805.caption: Freeipa Logfile: Max Age
805.description: Maximum age of the ipa-healthcheck result in hours. An older result means that the daily run no longer happens.

806.caption: Freeipa Logfile: No Perfdata?
806.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

807.caption: Freeipa Logfile: Warning
807.description: Least severe ipa-healthcheck result that returns WARNING. Each result includes everything more severe than itself, and a result that `--critical` already covers returns CRITICAL instead. Case-sensitive. `none` lets no result return WARNING. Example: `--warning=ERROR`.

809.caption: FS Inodes: Brief?
809.description: Hide the rows that are within the thresholds and show only those in a WARN or CRIT state. Perfdata and alerting are unaffected: every item still emits performance data and still drives the overall check state, so this is safe to leave on.

810.caption: FS Inodes: Critical
810.description: CRIT threshold in percent. Supports Nagios ranges.

811.caption: FS Inodes: Ignore
811.description: Any item matching this Python regex will be ignored. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `(?i)linuxfabrik` for a case-insensitive match.

813.caption: FS Inodes: Match
813.description: Filter by this Python regular expression. Case-sensitive by default; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching. Can be specified multiple times. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second). Examples: `(?i)example` to match "example" regardless of case. `^(?!.*example).*$` to match any string except "example" (negative lookahead).

814.caption: FS Inodes: No Match Severity
814.description: State to report when no item matches the filters and nothing is checked.

815.caption: FS Inodes: No Perfdata?

827.caption: FS RO: Extend Ignore Fstype
827.description: Filesystem type to ignore, appended to the default or the `--ignore-fstype` list. Case-sensitive. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--extend-ignore-fstype=iso9660`.

828.caption: FS RO: Ignore
828.description: Mount point prefix to ignore. All mount points starting with this value will be skipped. Replaces the default list, use `--extend-ignore` to append to it. Case-sensitive. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--ignore=/sys/fs` ignores `/sys/fs/cgroup` and similar. Default: /dev/loop, /proc, /run/credentials, /snap, /sys/fs, /var/lib/docker/containers.

829.description: Filesystem type to ignore, as shown in the third column of `/proc/mounts`. Replaces the default list, use `--extend-ignore-fstype` to append to it. Case-sensitive. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--ignore-fstype=squashfs --ignore-fstype=lustre`. Default: ramfs, squashfs.

1228.caption: Huawei Dorado Port: Link Down Severity

1229.description: Limit to ports. Filter by this Python regular expression. Case-sensitive by default; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching. Can be specified multiple times. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second). Examples: `(?i)example` to match "example" regardless of case. `^(?!.*example).*$` to match any string except "example" (negative lookahead). The regex is anchored at the start of the string (Python `re.match`) and is matched against the port identifier, its location and its name, so prefix with `.*` to match anywhere.

1230.description: Verify the TLS certificate against the system trust store, overriding the insecure default of this check. Use it once the endpoint presents a publicly trusted certificate, or once its CA has been added to the system trust store.

1231.description: State to report when no item matches the filters and nothing is checked.

1232.caption: Huawei Dorado Port: No Perfdata?
1232.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

1233.caption: Huawei Dorado Port: No Proxy?
1233.description: Do not use a proxy, not even one the environment names. Overrides `--proxy`.

2041.caption: Lynis: Audit Timeout
2041.description: Seconds to wait for the audit of a single host to finish.

2042.caption: Lynis: Configfile

2043.caption: Lynis: Connect Timeout

2044.caption: Lynis: Critical
2044.description: CRIT threshold for the per-host hardening index (0-100). Supports Nagios ranges. Empty by default, because a daily hardening scan is posture drift, not a time-critical event that should page someone at night.

2046.caption: Lynis: Host
2046.description: Target host to audit. Can be specified multiple times. Takes precedence over --network and --interface. If none of the three is specified, the subnet of the default interface is scanned.

2047.caption: Lynis: Identity
2047.description: SSH: File from which the identity (private key) for public key authentication is read. You can also specify a public key file to use the corresponding private key that is loaded in ssh-agent(1) when the private key file is not present locally. The default is `~/.ssh/id_dsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ecdsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ecdsa_sk`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_sk` and `~/.ssh/id_rsa`. Identity files may also be specified on a per-host basis in the configuration file. It is possible to have multiple --identity options (and multiple identities specified in configuration files). If no certificates have been explicitly specified by the CertificateFile directive, ssh will also try to load certificate information from the filename obtained by appending `-cert.pub` to identity filenames.

2048.caption: Lynis: Interface
2048.description: Network interface whose subnet is scanned. Ignored when --host or --network is given. If not specified, the default interface (the one carrying the default route) is used. Example: `--interface=eth0`

2049.caption: Lynis: IPv4?
2049.description: SSH: Forces ssh to use IPv4 addresses only.

2050.caption: Lynis: IPv6?
2050.description: SSH: Forces ssh to use IPv6 addresses only.

2051.caption: Lynis: Lynis Auditor
2051.description: Name of the auditor to record in the report (lynis `--auditor`). If not specified, lynis uses its own default.

2052.caption: Lynis: Lynis Option
2052.description: Additional raw option to pass to the remote `lynis audit system` call, for options that have no dedicated parameter here. Options that take a path are not passed on, and an option may only contain letters, digits, spaces and `._:=-`. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--lynis-option=--no-plugins`

2053.caption: Lynis: Lynis Profile
2053.description: Additional profile file for the audit (lynis `--profile`), read on top of lynis' own `default.prf` and `custom.prf`. The path is resolved on the target host. If not specified, lynis uses only its own profiles.

2054.caption: Lynis: Lynis Skip Test
2054.description: Lynis test ID to skip (passed to lynis as `skip-test`), for exceptions controlled from the monitoring configuration. Can be specified multiple times. Host-specific exceptions belong in the host's own `/etc/lynis/custom.prf` instead. Example: `--lynis-skip-test=MAIL-8818`

2055.caption: Lynis: Lynis Source
2055.description: Path to a self-contained lynis directory (the directory that contains the `lynis` executable next to its `include`, `db` and `plugins` subdirectories). This is the copy that gets pushed to and run on every target host. If not specified, a self-contained copy is assembled from the local lynis installation.

2056.caption: Lynis: Lynis Test
2056.description: Only run these lynis tests (lynis `--tests`). Can be specified multiple times. If not specified, all tests are run. Example: `--lynis-test=SSH-7408 --lynis-test=KRNL-5820`

2057.caption: Lynis: Lynis Test Category
2057.description: Only run lynis tests of this category (lynis `--tests-from-category`). lynis runs one category at a time. If not specified, all categories are run. Example: `--lynis-test-category=security`

2058.caption: Lynis: Lynis Test Group
2058.description: Only run lynis tests of these groups (lynis `--tests-from-group`). Can be specified multiple times. If not specified, all groups are run. Example: `--lynis-test-group=ssh --lynis-test-group=kernel`

2059.caption: Lynis: Max Workers
2059.description: Maximum number of hosts to audit in parallel in the network scan.

2060.caption: Lynis: Network

2064.caption: Lynis: Port
2064.description: SSH: Port to connect to on the remote host. This can be specified on a per-host basis in the configuration file.

2065.caption: Lynis: Quiet?

2120.description: Any item matching this Python regex will be ignored. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `(?i)linuxfabrik` for a case-insensitive match.

2121.caption: Md Raid: Journal Severity
2121.description: State to report when a parity array (RAID 4, RAID 5, RAID 6) that keeps a write journal has lost it. Such an array reports every member in sync and cannot be written to, and a buffered write to it is reported as having succeeded and then thrown away.

2123.caption: Md Raid: Match
2123.description: Filter by this Python regular expression. Case-sensitive by default; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching. Can be specified multiple times. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second). Examples: `(?i)example` to match "example" regardless of case. `^(?!.*example).*$` to match any string except "example" (negative lookahead).

2124.caption: Md Raid: Member Severity
2124.description: State to report when the kernel says a member device wants replacing, has seen a write error, or has bad blocks that are not acknowledged yet. None of the three reaches /proc/mdstat, so an array carrying one of them still reads as complete.

2125.caption: Md Raid: Mirror Mismatch Severity
2125.description: State to report when a consistency check found inconsistent sectors on a mirrored array (RAID 1, RAID 10). A page written while the check reads it, and above all a swap area, produce differences between the copies that nothing ever reads back, which is why this defaults to not alerting.

2126.caption: Md Raid: Mismatch Severity
2126.description: State to report when a consistency check found inconsistent sectors on a parity array (RAID 4, RAID 5, RAID 6). On such an array the difference points at hardware rather than at the way the data was written.

2127.caption: Md Raid: No Arrays Severity
2127.description: State to report when the host runs no software RAID array at all. An array is assembled from the superblocks on its members at every boot, so an array that used to be here and is gone is worth looking at.

2128.caption: Md Raid: No Match Severity
2128.description: State to report when no item matches the filters and nothing is checked.

2129.caption: Md Raid: No Perfdata?

2130.caption: Md Raid: Severity
2130.description: Severity for alerting. Applies to an array that is running on fewer members than it was built for, so it has lost the redundancy it is meant to provide, and to a member the kernel threw out that is still attached to an array a spare has already brought back to its full width.

2131.caption: Md Raid: Spares
2131.description: Number of spare devices an array is expected to hold. A bare count applies to every array, `array=count` pins one array and wins over the bare count. The array is named by its kernel device or by the name it was created under. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--spares=1` on a host where every array carries one hot spare. Example: `--spares=md0=1 --spares=md1=0` where only the first one does.

2132.caption: Md Raid: Spares Severity
2132.description: State to report when an array holds fewer spare devices than --spares says it should. Without a spare the next member the kernel throws out leaves the array degraded until somebody puts a disk in.

2210.caption: Multipath: Critical
2210.description: CRIT threshold for the percentage of the expected paths that are usable, compared as a Nagios range. Supports Nagios ranges. Example: `--critical=1:` alerts only once a map has no usable path left.

2211.caption: Multipath: Expected Paths
2211.description: Expected number of paths per multipath map. A LUN in a fabric normally has the same number of paths as every other one, so one value covers the whole host and catches a path that disappeared from a map entirely, which comparing a map against itself cannot. `--map` pins a single map that has a different number. Example: `--expected-paths=4` on a host with two HBAs and two controllers.

2212.caption: Multipath: Ignore
2212.description: Any item matching this Python regex will be ignored. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `(?i)linuxfabrik` for a case-insensitive match.

2214.caption: Multipath: Map
2214.description: Check this multipath map and, optionally, the number of paths it is expected to have, written as `name=count`. The name is the alias where the host uses one, and the WWID otherwise. Without `=count` the map is graded against `--expected-paths`, and against its own number of paths where that is not given either. Can be specified multiple times; if given at least once, only the named maps are checked. Example: `--map=mpatha=4` alerts when the `mpatha` map does not have its four paths, even after one of them disappeared from the map entirely. Example: `--map=mpathb` checks `mpathb` against the paths it currently has.

2215.caption: Multipath: Marginal Severity
2215.description: State to report for a path multipathd has declared marginal, which means it went up and down often enough that the daemon keeps it out of the normal path groups.

2216.caption: Multipath: No Maps Severity
2216.description: State to report when multipathd holds no map at all. A map whose last path disappears is flushed rather than kept with zero paths, so this is not necessarily a host without multipathed storage.

2217.caption: Multipath: No Match Severity
2217.description: State to report when no item matches the filters and nothing is checked.

2218.caption: Multipath: No Perfdata?

2220.caption: Multipath: Warning
2220.description: WARN threshold for the percentage of the expected paths that are usable, compared as a Nagios range. Supports Nagios ranges. Example: `--warning=60:` tolerates losing up to 40% of the paths before warning.

2244.caption: MySQL Database Metrics: Critical
2244.description: CRIT threshold for the size of a single table (data + index). Supports Nagios ranges with size qualifiers, for example `10G`, `5G:`, `@1G:10G`. Default: report only (no alerting).

2245.caption: MySQL Database Metrics: Defaults File
2245.description: MySQL/MariaDB cnf file to read user, host and password from. Example: `--defaults-file=/var/spool/icinga2/.my.cnf`.

2246.caption: MySQL Database Metrics: Defaults Group
2246.description: Group/section to read from in the cnf file.

2247.caption: MySQL Database Metrics: Ignore
2247.description: Ignore tables whose name matches this Python regular expression. Matched against the fully qualified table identifier `schema.table`, so one pattern can drop a whole schema or a single table. Excluded tables contribute to no aggregate and to no check; system schemas are skipped unconditionally. Case-sensitive by default; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching. Can be specified multiple times.

2249.caption: MySQL Database Metrics: Match
2249.description: Only check tables whose name matches this Python regular expression. Matched against the fully qualified table identifier `schema.table`. A schema without any table cannot match, so it drops out of the report while this is given. Case-sensitive by default; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching. Can be specified multiple times. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second).

2250.caption: MySQL Database Metrics: No Perfdata?
2250.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

2252.description: Number of largest tables (by data + index size) to list.

2253.caption: MySQL Database Metrics: Warning
2253.description: WARN threshold for the size of a single table (data + index). Supports Nagios ranges with size qualifiers, for example `10G`, `5G:`, `@1G:10G`. Default: report only (no alerting).

2264.description: Ignore indexes whose name matches this Python regular expression. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second).

2267.caption: MySQL Index Health: Min Uptime Hours
2267.description: Minimum server uptime (in hours) before the plugin starts evaluating findings. Performance Schema counters reset on every server restart, so a freshly booted server has no record of which indexes are read or unused; alerting on that data would produce false positives. Below the threshold the plugin reports OK with an info hint. Example: `--min-uptime-hours=48`.

2268.caption: MySQL Index Health: No Perfdata?
2268.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

2270.caption: MySQL Index Health: Warning Redundant
2270.description: WARN threshold for the number of matching items. Applies to redundant indexes. Supports Nagios ranges. Example: `--warning-redundant=0`. Default: not evaluated, the redundant indexes are only listed.

2271.caption: MySQL Index Health: Warning Unused
2271.description: WARN threshold for the number of matching items. Applies to unused indexes. Supports Nagios ranges. Example: `--warning-unused=10`. Default: not evaluated, the unused indexes are only listed.

2272.caption: MySQL Innodb Buffer Pool Size: Always OK?

2273.caption: MySQL Innodb Buffer Pool Size: Critical
2273.description: CRIT threshold for how far the checkpoint has run through the redo log, in percent of `Innodb_checkpoint_max_age`. From 100 InnoDB puts a synchronous wait into every write operation, and a redo log that is too small sits pinned there under load. Only evaluated on a server that publishes its checkpoint age. Supports Nagios ranges.

2277.caption: MySQL Innodb Buffer Pool Size: Timeout

2278.caption: MySQL Innodb Buffer Pool Size: Warning
2278.description: WARN threshold for how far the checkpoint has run through the redo log, in percent of `Innodb_checkpoint_max_age`. At 87.5 InnoDB starts flushing pages ahead to keep the checkpoint moving. Only evaluated on a server that publishes its checkpoint age. Supports Nagios ranges.

2279.caption: MySQL Innodb Log Waits: Always OK?

2280.caption: MySQL Innodb Log Waits: Critical
2280.description: Threshold for redo log pressure, in percent of the point where InnoDB starts to flush synchronously and holds back writing sessions.

2281.caption: MySQL Innodb Log Waits: Defaults File

2289.description: Minimum server uptime (in hours) before the plugin starts evaluating the rate of joins without indexes. The rate is a per-day average over the uptime, so a freshly booted server extrapolates a handful of joins to hundreds per day. Below the threshold the rate is reported but does not raise WARN. Example: `--min-uptime-hours=48`.

2290.caption: MySQL Joins: No Perfdata?

2292.caption: MySQL Logfile: Aborted Connections Critical
2292.description: Number of connections the clients dropped within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. Counted per client host, so one application falling over reaches it while the same number spread over a fleet does not. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--aborted-connections-critical=500`.

2293.caption: MySQL Logfile: Aborted Connections Warning
2293.description: Number of connections the clients dropped within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. Counted per client host, so one application falling over reaches it while the same number spread over a fleet does not. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--aborted-connections-warning=50`.

2294.caption: MySQL Logfile: Access Denied Critical
2294.description: Number of logins the server turned away within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--access-denied-critical=200`.

2295.caption: MySQL Logfile: Access Denied Warning
2295.description: Number of logins the server turned away within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. Counted per source address, so a run against one account from one host reaches it while the same number of typos across a fleet does not. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--access-denied-warning=1`.

2297.caption: MySQL Logfile: Cache Expire
2297.description: The amount of time after which the credential/data cache expires, in minutes.

2298.caption: MySQL Logfile: Defaults File
2298.description: MySQL/MariaDB cnf file to read user, host and password from. Has to be a regular file that belongs to the account running the check (the one calling sudo); any other is not used. Example: `--defaults-file=/var/spool/icinga2/.my.cnf`.

2299.caption: MySQL Logfile: Defaults Group
2299.description: Group/section to read from in the cnf file.

2301.caption: MySQL Logfile: Icinga Callback?
2301.description: Ask the monitoring server whether the service running this check is acknowledged. Where it is, what this run reports is remembered as already handled, so it no longer raises an alert on the following runs. Requires `--icinga-url`, `--icinga-username`, `--icinga-password` and `--icinga-service-name`.

2303.caption: MySQL Logfile: Icinga Service Name
2303.description: Unique name of the service running this check, as the monitoring server knows it. Take it from the `__name` service attribute. Example: `monitoring-server!my-service-name`.

2306.caption: MySQL Logfile: Ignore
2306.description: Ignore a log line matching this Python regular expression. The log line is lowercased before matching, so write the pattern in lowercase (or use the `(?i)` flag). Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--ignore='(?i)linuxfabrik'`.

2307.caption: MySQL Logfile: Insecure?
2307.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes. This option explicitly allows insecure SSL connections.

2308.caption: MySQL Logfile: Lookback
2308.description: Logins the server turned away are counted within this window rather than reported one by one. Time window in seconds to look back over, ending at the moment of the run. Only what falls within it is counted, so what is reported is how often something happened lately rather than a total that keeps growing for as long as the source is kept. Example: `--lookback=3600`.

2309.caption: MySQL Logfile: Match
2309.description: Only consider a log line matching this Python regular expression. The log line is lowercased before matching, so write the pattern in lowercase (or use the `(?i)` flag). Can be specified multiple times. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second). Example: `--match='innodb'`.

2310.caption: MySQL Logfile: No Insecure?
2310.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes. Verify the TLS certificate against the system trust store, overriding the insecure default of this check. Use it once the endpoint presents a publicly trusted certificate, or once its CA has been added to the system trust store.

2311.caption: MySQL Logfile: No Match Severity
2311.description: State to report when no item matches the filters and nothing is checked.

2312.caption: MySQL Logfile: No Per Source?
2312.description: Judge a rate by everything that arrived within the window, whatever source the lines name. Use this where the log reaches this check through something that rewrites or drops the address of the peer, or where every source is as interesting as the next.

2313.caption: MySQL Logfile: No Perfdata?
2313.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

2314.caption: MySQL Logfile: No Proxy?
2314.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes. Do not use a proxy, not even one the environment names. Overrides `--proxy`.

2315.caption: MySQL Logfile: Per Source?
2315.description: Judge a rate by the busiest single source address rather than by everything that arrived. A handful of failures from one address within the window is somebody working on this host; the same number spread over as many addresses is the background of an open network going past, and only the first is worth reporting. Lines that name no source are counted together as one, so a burst of those still reports.

2317.caption: MySQL Logfile: Proxy
2317.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes. Proxy to reach the target through. The scheme defaults to `http` when omitted. Overrides the proxy the environment names (`http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `all_proxy`) together with the exceptions it lists in `no_proxy`, and is itself overridden by `--no-proxy`. Without either parameter the environment applies. Credentials belong into the environment variable rather than here, because a command-line argument is visible to every user on the host. Example: `--proxy=http://proxy.example.com:3128`.

2318.caption: MySQL Logfile: Server Log
2318.description: Log source to read from. Accepts a file path, `docker:CONTAINER`, `podman:CONTAINER`, `kubectl:CONTAINER` or `systemd:UNITNAME`. Can be specified multiple times, and everything named is then read as one window; a source named twice is read once. If omitted, the check first probes `performance_schema.error_log` (MySQL 8.0.22+) and then falls back to the file from `log_error`, read along with the journal of the database unit; what the two share is counted once.

2321.caption: MySQL Long Queries: Critical
2321.description: Query runtime in seconds that triggers CRIT. Supports Nagios ranges. Example: `--critical=60`.

2322.caption: MySQL Long Queries: Defaults File
2322.description: MySQL/MariaDB cnf file to read user, host and password from. Example: `--defaults-file=/var/spool/icinga2/.my.cnf`.

2323.caption: MySQL Long Queries: Defaults Group
2323.description: Group/section to read from in the cnf file.

2324.caption: MySQL Long Queries: Ignore
2324.description: Regex applied to the running statement. Matching queries are ignored (e.g. `--ignore=^mysqldump` to exclude backup runs). Repeat the flag for multiple patterns. Example: `--ignore=ANALYZE --ignore=^mysqldump`

2326.caption: MySQL Long Queries: No Perfdata?
2326.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

2328.caption: MySQL Long Queries: Warning
2328.description: Query runtime in seconds that triggers WARN. Supports Nagios ranges. Example: `--warning=15`.

2330.caption: MySQL Memory: Critical
2330.description: CRIT threshold for the percentage of physical RAM consumed by the reached MySQL memory footprint (server_buffers + per_thread_buffers * Max_used_connections + Performance Schema + Galera GCache). Supports Nagios ranges.

2331.caption: MySQL Memory: Defaults File
2331.description: MySQL/MariaDB cnf file to read user, host and password from. Example: `--defaults-file=/var/spool/icinga2/.my.cnf`.

2333.description: Append a full memory breakdown table to the output (each contributing buffer + the calculation that produces server_buffers, per_thread_buffers, max_used_memory and max_peak_memory). Useful when a WARNING/CRITICAL fires and you need to see which buffer dominates the footprint.

2334.caption: MySQL Memory: No Perfdata?
2334.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

2336.caption: MySQL Memory: Warning
2336.description: WARN threshold for the percentage of physical RAM consumed by the reached MySQL memory footprint. Supports Nagios ranges.

2338.caption: MySQL Open Files: Critical
2338.description: CRIT threshold in percent. Supports Nagios ranges.

2339.caption: MySQL Open Files: Defaults File
2339.description: MySQL/MariaDB cnf file to read user, host and password from. Example: `--defaults-file=/var/spool/icinga2/.my.cnf`.

2340.caption: MySQL Open Files: Defaults Group
2340.description: Group/section to read from in the cnf file.

2341.caption: MySQL Open Files: No Perfdata?
2341.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

2345.caption: MySQL Perf Metrics: Defaults File
2345.description: MySQL/MariaDB cnf file to read user, host and password from. Example: `--defaults-file=/var/spool/icinga2/.my.cnf`.

2346.caption: MySQL Perf Metrics: Defaults Group
2346.description: Group/section to read from in the cnf file.

2347.caption: MySQL Perf Metrics: Ignore Innodb Snapshot Isolation?
2347.description: Suppress the hint about `innodb_snapshot_isolation` being `OFF` under `REPEATABLE-READ`. The hint never changes the state. Use it where an application connecting to this server cannot retry a transaction that was rolled back with error 1020, so the admin has no way to turn the variable on.

2348.caption: MySQL Perf Metrics: No Perfdata?
2348.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

2349.caption: MySQL Perf Metrics: Storage Type
2349.description: Storage type of the MySQL data directory. Drives the `innodb_flush_neighbors` and `innodb_io_capacity` checks. `auto` reads `/sys/block/*/queue/rotational` on the same host and feeds `innodb_flush_neighbors` only; `ssd` or `hdd` overrides the detection (use when running from a remote monitoring host via TCP, or on virtualised/network-backed storage such as Ceph or cloud volumes where the rotational flag is unreliable); `skip` disables both storage-type checks entirely. The `innodb_io_capacity` check only runs when `ssd` is set explicitly. Example: `--storage-type=ssd`.

2352.caption: MySQL Query: Critical
2352.description: CRIT threshold as a Nagios range expression.

2353.caption: MySQL Query: Critical Query
2353.description: `SELECT` statement whose result is checked against `--critical`. If the result contains more than one column, the row count is used. Otherwise the single returned value is used.

2354.caption: MySQL Query: Defaults File
2354.description: MySQL/MariaDB cnf file to read user, host and password from. Example: `--defaults-file=/var/spool/icinga2/.my.cnf`.

2355.caption: MySQL Query: Defaults Group

2356.caption: MySQL Query: No Perfdata?
2356.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

2358.caption: MySQL Query: Warning
2358.description: WARN threshold as a Nagios range expression.

2577.caption: Nextcloud Version: Check Minor?
2577.description: Alert when a new major.minor release is available, even if the current version is not yet EOL. Example: running v26.2 (not yet EOL) and v26.3 is available.

2578.caption: Nextcloud Version: Check Patch?
2578.description: Alert when a new major.minor.patch release is available, even if the current version is not yet EOL. Example: running v26.2.7 (not yet EOL) and v26.2.8 is available.

2581.caption: Nextcloud Version: No Proxy?
2581.description: Do not use a proxy, not even one the environment names. Overrides `--proxy`.

2582.caption: Nextcloud Version: Offset Eol
2582.description: Alert n days before ("-30") or after an EOL date ("30" or "+30").

2583.caption: Nextcloud Version: Path
2583.description: Local path to the Nextcloud installation, typically the web server document root.

2584.caption: Nextcloud Version: Proxy
2584.description: Proxy to reach the target through. The scheme defaults to `http` when omitted. Overrides the proxy the environment names (`http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `all_proxy`) together with the exceptions it lists in `no_proxy`, and is itself overridden by `--no-proxy`. Without either parameter the environment applies. Credentials belong into the environment variable rather than here, because a command-line argument is visible to every user on the host. Example: `--proxy=http://proxy.example.com:3128`.

2586.caption: Nextcloud Version: Unreachable Severity
2586.description: State to report when the online source is unreachable. What is used instead - bundled offline data, a cached copy, or nothing at all - is named in the output, and a clean result then only covers what that fallback could confirm.

2588.caption: Nfs Exports: Brief?
2588.description: Hide the rows that are within the thresholds and show only those in a WARN or CRIT state. Perfdata and alerting are unaffected: every item still emits performance data and still drives the overall check state, so this is safe to leave on.

2589.caption: Nfs Exports: Etab
2589.description: Path to the export table the server serves, which is where the state directory of the NFS utilities was moved to if it was moved at all.

2590.caption: Nfs Exports: Ignore
2590.description: Any item matching this Python regex will be ignored. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `(?i)linuxfabrik` for a case-insensitive match.

2591.caption: Nfs Exports: Match
2591.description: Filter by this Python regular expression. Case-sensitive by default; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching. Can be specified multiple times. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second). Examples: `(?i)example` to match "example" regardless of case. `^(?!.*example).*$` to match any string except "example" (negative lookahead).

2592.caption: Nfs Exports: Missing Path Severity
2592.description: State to report for an export whose path does not exist. The server keeps serving it, and a client that has it mounted gets a stale file handle.

2593.caption: Nfs Exports: No Match Severity
2593.description: State to report when no item matches the filters and nothing is checked.

2594.caption: Nfs Exports: No Perfdata?
2594.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

2595.caption: Nfs Exports: Not Exported Severity
2595.description: State to report for an export the configuration asks for and the server does not serve. Usually `exportfs -ra` has not been run since the entry was added, or it refused the entry; a client cannot mount such a share at all.

2596.caption: Nfs Exports: Timeout
2596.description: How long the export paths get to answer before they are reported as unreachable. Only a path on a network filesystem ever needs it: one whose server has stopped answering does not fail, it blocks. Every path is looked at at the same time and they share one deadline, so this is the runtime of the whole check and not a budget per path.

2597.caption: Nfs Exports: Unconfigured Severity
2597.description: State to report for an export the server serves and the configuration does not ask for. Cluster software that creates its exports at runtime looks exactly like this, which is why it does not alert by default.

2599.caption: Nfs Mounts: Brief?
2599.description: Hide the rows that are within the thresholds and show only those in a WARN or CRIT state. Perfdata and alerting are unaffected: every item still emits performance data and still drives the overall check state, so this is safe to leave on.

2600.caption: Nfs Mounts: Error Severity
2600.description: State to report for a mount that answers with an error other than a stale file handle, for example the I/O error a `soft` mount reports once it has given up on its server.

2601.caption: Nfs Mounts: Hung Severity
2601.description: State to report for a mount that does not answer within --timeout. A `hard` mount blocks instead of failing, so this is what an unreachable server looks like, and a process waiting on such a mount only gets out of that wait by being killed.

2602.caption: Nfs Mounts: Ignore

2607.caption: Nfs Mounts: Stale Severity
2607.description: State to report for a mount that answers with a stale file handle. The export it points at is gone, and the mount does not recover on its own.

2608.caption: Nfs Mounts: Timeout
2608.description: Network timeout in seconds. Every mount is asked at the same time and they share one deadline, so this is the runtime of the whole check and not a budget per mount.

Time window in seconds to look back over, ending at the moment of the run. Only what falls within it is counted, so what is reported is how often something happened lately rather than a total that keeps growing for as long as the source is kept. Example: `--lookback=3600`.

2883.caption: PHP-FPM Logfile: Match

Verify the TLS certificate against the system trust store, overriding the insecure default of this check. Use it once the endpoint presents a publicly trusted certificate, or once its CA has been added to the system trust store.

2891.caption: PHP-FPM Logfile: Server Log
2891.description: Log source to read from. Accepts a file path, `docker:CONTAINER`, `podman:CONTAINER`, `kubectl:CONTAINER` or `systemd:UNITNAME`. Can be specified multiple times, and everything named is then read as one window; a source named twice is read once. If omitted, the check reads the `error_log` directive of the PHP-FPM configuration, falls back to the common locations of the distributions, and reads the journal of the PHP-FPM unit along with it; what the two share is counted once. It also reads the `error_log` file every pool names for the messages of PHP itself. Example: `--server-log=systemd:php-fpm.service`.

2895.caption: PHP-FPM Logfile: Spawn Pressure Warning

2901.caption: PHP-FPM Ping: No Proxy?
2901.description: Do not use a proxy, not even one the environment names. Overrides `--proxy`.

2902.caption: PHP-FPM Ping: Proxy
2902.description: Proxy to reach the target through. The scheme defaults to `http` when omitted. Overrides the proxy the environment names (`http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `all_proxy`) together with the exceptions it lists in `no_proxy`, and is itself overridden by `--no-proxy`. Without either parameter the environment applies. Credentials belong into the environment variable rather than here, because a command-line argument is visible to every user on the host. Example: `--proxy=http://proxy.example.com:3128`.

2908.caption: PHP-FPM Status: Critical
2908.description: CRIT threshold for pool saturation (active processes / total processes), in percent. Applies to static pools only - on dynamic and ondemand pools, `total processes` is the live worker count, so 100% is a transient state and the plugin uses `listen queue > 0` as the saturation signal instead.

2909.caption: PHP-FPM Status: Critical SlowReq
2909.description: CRIT threshold for the number of NEW slow requests seen since the previous check run.

2910.caption: PHP-FPM Status: Insecure?

2912.caption: PHP-FPM Status: No Perfdata?

2913.caption: PHP-FPM Status: No Proxy?

2914.caption: PHP-FPM Status: Proxy
2914.description: Proxy to reach the target through. The scheme defaults to `http` when omitted. Overrides the proxy the environment names (`http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `all_proxy`) together with the exceptions it lists in `no_proxy`, and is itself overridden by `--no-proxy`. Without either parameter the environment applies. Credentials belong into the environment variable rather than here, because a command-line argument is visible to every user on the host. 2915.caption: PHP-FPM Status: Severity
2915.description: Severity for alerting. Applied to pools that are unreachable or whose status JSON cannot be parsed. Saturation and slow-request thresholds are unaffected.

2917.caption: PHP-FPM Status: URL
2917.description: PHP-FPM status page URL. Can be specified multiple times to check several pools on the same host; each URL is treated as an independent pool. Basic authentication may be embedded in the URL as `http://user:password@host/pool-status`; the credentials are stripped from the request URL and sent via the `Authorization` header. Default: http://localhost/fpm-status

2918.caption: PHP-FPM Status: Warning
2918.description: WARN threshold for pool saturation (active processes / total processes), in percent. Applies to static pools only - on dynamic and ondemand pools, `total processes` is the live worker count, so 100% is a transient state and the plugin uses `listen queue > 0` as the saturation signal instead.

2919.caption: PHP-FPM Status: Warning SlowReq
2919.description: WARN threshold for the number of NEW slow requests seen since the previous check run.

2921.caption: PHP Status: Config
2921.description: PHP ini "key=value" pair to check. The whole value is compared, case-insensitive. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--config=memory_limit=128M`. Without it, only an unset `date.timezone` is reported.

2922.caption: PHP Status: Critical
2922.description: CRIT threshold for OPcache memory and key usage, in percent.

2924.caption: PHP Status: Extend Module
2924.description: PHP module name to check, matched against the start of each module `php --modules` lists, appended to the default or the `--module` list. Case-insensitive. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--extend-module=mbstring`.

2925.caption: PHP Status: Ignore Multiple Masters?
2925.description: Do not warn when more than one PHP-FPM master is running. Use this on hosts where you intentionally run several PHP-FPM services and monitor each one with its own check.

2926.caption: PHP Status: Insecure?
2926.description: This option explicitly allows insecure SSL connections.

2927.caption: PHP Status: Module
2927.description: PHP module name to check, matched against the start of each module `php --modules` lists. Replaces the default list, use `--extend-module` to append to it. Case-insensitive. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--module=json --module=mbstring`. Default: calendar, Core, ctype, date, exif, fileinfo, filter, ftp, gettext, hash, iconv, json, libxml, openssl, pcntl, pcre, Phar, readline, Reflection, session, sockets, SPL, standard, tokenizer, xml, zlib.

2928.caption: PHP Status: No Perfdata?

2980.caption: Podman Container: Critical Restarts
2980.description: CRIT threshold for the number of automatic restarts a container has performed, compared as a Nagios range. Example: `--critical-restarts=5` alerts when a container has restarted more than 5 times. By default, the restart count is reported but not alerted on.

2981.caption: Podman Container: Critical Uptime
2981.description: CRIT threshold for the container uptime in a human-readable format (s = seconds, m = minutes, h = hours, D = days, W = weeks, M = months, Y = years). Supports Nagios ranges. Example: `5m:` alerts if a running container has been up for less than 5 minutes (catches a crash-looping or flapping container). By default, the uptime is reported but not alerted on.

2982.caption: Podman Container: Full Name?
2982.description: Use the full container name, for example `traefik_traefik.2.1idw12p2yqp`. Without this flag, the name is shortened after the replica number.

2983.caption: Podman Container: Ignore
2983.description: Ignore containers whose name matches this Python regular expression. Matched against the full container name, even when the displayed name is shortened (see --full-name). Case-sensitive by default; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching. Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--ignore="^k8s_"` to skip Kubernetes pod infrastructure containers. Example: `--ignore="(?i)test"` (case-insensitive) to skip any container with "test" in its name.

2984.caption: Podman Container: Match
2984.description: Only check containers whose name matches this Python regular expression. Matched against the full container name, even when the displayed name is shortened (see --full-name). Case-sensitive by default; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching. Can be specified multiple times. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second). Example: `--match="^traefik$"` to pin a service to one specific container. Example: `--match="(?i)^web"` (case-insensitive) to check every web container.

2985.caption: Podman Container: No Match Severity
2985.description: State to report when no item matches the filters and nothing is checked.

2986.caption: Podman Container: No Perfdata?
2986.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

2987.caption: Podman Container: Status
2987.description: Desired container status. Podman reports one of `created`, `initialized`, `running`, `paused`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `exited`, `removing` and `unknown`. A container whose status differs is reported as CRITICAL. If not specified, the status is reported but not alerted on.

2989.caption: Podman Container: User
2989.description: Inspect the rootless containers of this user instead of those visible to the executing user. Podman keeps each user's rootless containers in that user's own storage, so root (the monitoring user runs the check via sudo) does not see them. With --user, the check runs podman as that user. Requires the right to `sudo -u <user>` (root has this by default), and the user needs a subordinate UID range in /etc/subuid, as rootless Podman does. Example: `--user=rocketchat`.

2991.caption: Podman Container: Warning Uptime

3020.caption: Postfix Logfile: Aborted Connections Critical
3020.description: Number of conversations that ended before a message was handed over within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--aborted-connections-critical=5000`.

3021.caption: Postfix Logfile: Aborted Connections Warning
3021.description: Number of conversations that ended before a message was handed over within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. Every server answering on port 25 collects these all day, so this is meant to catch a scan starting and not the background noise. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--aborted-connections-warning=500`.

3023.caption: Postfix Logfile: Auth Failures Critical
3023.description: Number of failed SMTP logins within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--auth-failures-critical=200`.

3024.caption: Postfix Logfile: Auth Failures Warning
3024.description: Number of failed SMTP logins within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. Counted per source address, so a run against one mailbox from one host reaches it while the same number of typos across a fleet does not. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--auth-failures-warning=5`.

3025.caption: Postfix Logfile: Bounced Critical
3025.description: Number of deliveries given up on within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--bounced-critical=500`.

3026.caption: Postfix Logfile: Bounced Warning
3026.description: Number of deliveries given up on within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. On a host that only sends its own mail, every one of them is a message nobody will read; a server receiving from the internet bounces all day and wants this raised. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--bounced-warning=1`.

3027.caption: Postfix Logfile: Critical Level
3027.description: Least severe Postfix log level that returns CRITICAL. Each level includes everything more severe than itself, so `error` covers `fatal` and `panic` as well. Case-sensitive. `none` lets no level return CRITICAL, which leaves the events this check names as the only way to reach it. Example: `--critical-level=error`.

3028.caption: Postfix Logfile: Deferred Critical
3028.description: Number of deliveries put back into the queue within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--deferred-critical=500`.

3029.caption: Postfix Logfile: Deferred Warning
3029.description: Number of deliveries put back into the queue within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. A single one is a mailbox that is full; a burst of them is the next hop being down. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--deferred-warning=5`.

3030.caption: Postfix Logfile: Icinga Callback?
3030.description: Ask the monitoring server whether the service running this check is acknowledged. Where it is, what this run reports is remembered as already handled, so it no longer raises an alert on the following runs. Requires `--icinga-url`, `--icinga-username`, `--icinga-password` and `--icinga-service-name`.

3032.caption: Postfix Logfile: Icinga Service Name
3032.description: Unique name of the service running this check, as the monitoring server knows it. Take it from the `__name` service attribute. Example: `monitoring-server!my-service-name`.

3035.caption: Postfix Logfile: Ignore
3035.description: Ignore a log line matching this Python regular expression. The log line is lowercased before matching, so write the pattern in lowercase (or use the `(?i)` flag). Can be specified multiple times. Example: `--ignore='status=bounced'`.

3036.caption: Postfix Logfile: Insecure?
3036.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes, which is the only network connection this check opens. This option explicitly allows insecure SSL connections.

3037.caption: Postfix Logfile: Lookback
3037.description: Failed logins, rejected messages, aborted connections, deferred and bounced deliveries are counted within this window rather than reported one by one. Time window in seconds to look back over, ending at the moment of the run. Only what falls within it is counted, so what is reported is how often something happened lately rather than a total that keeps growing for as long as the source is kept. Example: `--lookback=3600`.

3038.caption: Postfix Logfile: Match
3038.description: Only consider a log line matching this Python regular expression. The log line is lowercased before matching, so write the pattern in lowercase (or use the `(?i)` flag). Can be specified multiple times. If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second). Example: `--match='postfix/smtpd'`.

3039.caption: Postfix Logfile: No Insecure?
3039.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes, which is the only network connection this check opens. Verify the TLS certificate against the system trust store, overriding the insecure default of this check. Use it once the endpoint presents a publicly trusted certificate, or once its CA has been added to the system trust store.

3040.caption: Postfix Logfile: No Match Severity
3040.description: State to report when no item matches the filters and nothing is checked.

3041.caption: Postfix Logfile: No Per Source?
3041.description: Judge a rate by everything that arrived within the window, whatever source the lines name. Use this where the log reaches this check through something that rewrites or drops the address of the peer, or where every source is as interesting as the next.

3042.caption: Postfix Logfile: No Perfdata?
3042.description: Suppress the performance data section from the output. The status message and the exit code are unaffected, so alerting keeps working while trending data is dropped.

3043.caption: Postfix Logfile: No Proxy?
3043.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes, which is the only network connection this check opens. Do not use a proxy, not even one the environment names. Overrides `--proxy`.

3044.caption: Postfix Logfile: Per Source?
3044.description: Judge a rate by the busiest single source address rather than by everything that arrived. A handful of failures from one address within the window is somebody working on this host; the same number spread over as many addresses is the background of an open network going past, and only the first is worth reporting. Lines that name no source are counted together as one, so a burst of those still reports.

3045.caption: Postfix Logfile: Proxy
3045.description: Applies to the connection to the monitoring server that `--icinga-callback` makes, which is the only network connection this check opens. Proxy to reach the target through. The scheme defaults to `http` when omitted. Overrides the proxy the environment names (`http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `all_proxy`) together with the exceptions it lists in `no_proxy`, and is itself overridden by `--no-proxy`. Without either parameter the environment applies. Credentials belong into the environment variable rather than here, because a command-line argument is visible to every user on the host. Example: `--proxy=http://proxy.example.com:3128`.

3046.caption: Postfix Logfile: Rejects Critical
3046.description: Number of messages the server turned away within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--rejects-critical=200`.

3047.caption: Postfix Logfile: Rejects Warning
3047.description: Number of messages the server turned away within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. Counted per source address. A server that answers the internet turns mail away all day and wants this raised. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--rejects-warning=50`.

3048.caption: Postfix Logfile: Relay Failures Critical
3048.description: Number of failed connections to the next hop within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--relay-failures-critical=500`.

3049.caption: Postfix Logfile: Relay Failures Warning
3049.description: Number of failed connections to the next hop within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. A host without an IPv6 route logs one for the AAAA record of its relay and delivers over IPv4 in the same second, so a single one is not a failure; a relay that is really down produces them by the dozen. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--relay-failures-warning=5`.

3050.caption: Postfix Logfile: Server Log
3050.description: Log source to read from. Accepts a file path, `docker:CONTAINER`, `podman:CONTAINER`, `kubectl:CONTAINER` or `systemd:UNITNAME`. Can be specified multiple times, and everything named is then read as one window; a source named twice is read once. If omitted, the check takes `maillog_file` from the Postfix configuration where it is set, falls back to the mail log of the distribution, and reads the journal of the Postfix unit along with it; what the two share is counted once. Example: `--server-log=systemd:postfix.service`.

3052.caption: Postfix Logfile: TLS Failures Critical
3052.description: Number of TLS connections that did not come off within `--lookback` that returns CRITICAL. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--tls-failures-critical=500`.

3053.caption: Postfix Logfile: TLS Failures Warning
3053.description: Number of TLS connections that did not come off within `--lookback` that returns WARNING. A single one is one remote server having a bad day; a server that answers the internet collects those all day. 0 turns the threshold off. Example: `--tls-failures-warning=5`.

3054.caption: Postfix Logfile: Warning Level
3054.description: Least severe Postfix log level that returns WARNING. Each level includes everything more severe than itself, and a level that `--critical-level` already covers returns CRITICAL instead. Case-sensitive. `none` lets no level return WARNING, which leaves the events this check names as the only way to reach it. Example: `--warning-level=error`.

3466.caption: RPM Updates: Critical
3466.description: Minimum number of pending security updates to trigger a CRITICAL. Counts the updates carrying a security advisory or coming from the Rocky Linux `security` repository (if enabled), within the scope of `--query`. Unset by default, so security updates raise a WARNING like any other update until a threshold is given. Example: `--critical=1`

3467.caption: RPM Updates: Grace Security
3467.description: How long a pending security update is tolerated before it counts towards the thresholds. Starts when the update is first seen, and starts over if the package drops off the list and comes back. A duration such as `12h`, `8D` or `2W`; `0D` disables the grace period.

3468.caption: RPM Updates: Grace Updates
3468.description: How long a pending update is tolerated before it counts towards the thresholds. Set this to cover the interval between two patch windows, so a host stays quiet about updates it has had no chance to install yet. Starts when the update is first seen, and starts over if the package drops off the list and comes back. A duration such as `12h`, `8D` or `2W`; `0D` disables the grace period.

3471.description: SQL WHERE clause to filter the list of available updates. Supports regular expressions via a REGEXP statement. See the README for a list of available columns. If specified, a list of matching updates is printed. Example: `--query='package like "bind9-%"'`.

3473.caption: RPM Updates: Warning

3479.caption: RPM Versionlock: Match

If both `--match` and `--ignore` are given, an item must match `--match` AND not match `--ignore` to be reported (include first, exclude second). Examples: `(?i)example` to match "example" regardless of case. `^(?!.*example).*$` to match any string except "example" (negative lookahead).

3533.caption: SNMP: Device
3533.description: CSV file containing the SNMP OIDs. A bare filename is looked up under the bundled `./device-oids` directory. An absolute path loads a CSV from anywhere on the filesystem, so the OID definitions can live outside the plugin directory. The recommended naming convention is `class-vendor-model.csv`. `any-any-any.csv` is a good starting point showing some features. The file is trusted input: its recalculation and threshold fields are evaluated as Python expressions, so it must be writable only by trusted, privileged users. The monitoring user (for example `icinga` or `nagios`) only needs read access. Example: `--device=switch-fs-s3900.csv`. Example: `--device=/etc/icinga2/snmp-devices/switch-fs-s3900.csv`.
